prompt: Why is FIXED burst plus EXOKAY response not enough evidence, by itself, to mark a coverage cross as structurally illegal?
expectedTakeaway: EXOKAY legality depends on the exclusive transaction context and response channel. A burst-type/response pair alone is insufficient to classify the scenario, so exclusions must be justified from the full transaction and the implemented exclusive-access support.
options: Because EXOKAY depends on exclusive-request context; the burst type and response value alone do not prove illegality.
Because every FIXED burst is automatically an exclusive access.
Because EXOKAY is a timing waveform that consumes two cycles.
Because FIXED bursts never produce a write or read response.
